statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in the current hour and Tail is held at the closed-venue floor of 5%. Stress rises to 56% because the Hormuz sequence produced a fresh step at roughly 03:03 UTC: the IRGC published a claim that its naval force struck a US unmanned surface vessel attempting to enter the strait. The target was unmanned and CENTCOM has not confirmed or denied the claim, which keeps the step below the casualty threshold that would justify a wider allowance. The scheduled 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen and the first full hour after it remain the two WATCH slots of this horizon.
recommendation: Tail holds a 5% closed-venue floor through the dormant weekend hours, lifts from the eleventh slot as a pre-auction gap allowance and reaches 14% in the final full hour of the halt, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green for the first nineteen published hours. The 22:00 UTC reopening hour and the first full hour after it are each scored at 20% Tail and therefore map to WATCH and yellow; together they form the only published danger window. The last three slots step back to 17%, 15% and 14% and to green on the assumption of an orderly two-way auction into a shortened Labor Day session. Stress runs from 56% down to a 54% low in the quiet Sunday hours, rebuilds to a 72% peak at the reopen and enters the high band from the seventeenth slot onward. Confidence declines from 85% to 72% as later slots rest on progressively older Friday-dated evidence.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 with about nineteen hours of the CME weekend halt left; the IRGC claimed a strike on a US unmanned surface vessel in Hormuz at roughly 03:03 UTC, lifting Stress to 56% while Tail stays on the closed-venue floor
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, after ranging between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that 215-point range, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September. That reopening hour and the first full hour after it are the two WATCH slots of this forecast.

The geopolitical sequence produced a new step during the current hour. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps published a statement, carried at about 03:03 UTC, saying its naval force struck an American unmanned surface vessel attempting to breach what it described as the restricted area of the Strait of Hormuz, and repeating a demand that the United States leave the region. This follows Saturday's exchange, in which US Central Command said it had permanently disabled two Iranian oil tankers and destroyed a third in retaliation for IRGC ballistic-missile fire toward an American carrier and destroyer, and the separate IRGC claim of hitting three tankers and three US-affiliated vessels. The new claim is an escalation, but the stated target was unmanned, no casualty has been reported, and CENTCOM has neither confirmed nor denied it. Under the risk definitions used here, an unresolved military exchange at a shipping chokepoint with a closed equity venue raises Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures an observable pathological price path and no price path can exist while the venue is shut.

The macro impulse into the halt is hawkish. August non-farm payrolls printed 162,000 against roughly 53,000 expected, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. The 2-year yield rose more than four basis points to 4.377%, its highest since January 2025, and the 10-year added more than two basis points to 4.784%; the Federal Reserve H.15 release dated 4 September carries 4.34% and 4.77% for the preceding business day. Reporting around the print described a labour market hot enough to give the Federal Reserve cover to raise rates at the September meeting, which falls outside this seven-day calendar. WTI settled at 91.48 dollars, up more than 9% on the week and its strongest weekly showing since mid-July, on Hormuz supply risk. Against that, the VIX closed at 14.53 inside a 13.80 to 14.58 range, an unusually calm volatility anchor for a week carrying an active naval conflict.

Cross-asset tone into the halt was rotational rather than one-way: semiconductors and semiconductor equipment led while application and infrastructure software fell, and the Nasdaq-100 rose while broader large-cap and industrial benchmarks did not. Dispersion of that kind reduces directional conviction and argues against the aligned-breadth condition that would amplify Tail. The shared Finviz cross-asset context file was collected at 01:22 UTC and is therefore older than the ninety-minute freshness threshold at this assessment time; it was read as stale supporting context only, is latest-session rather than live, and was not used as evidence of any current Nasdaq-100 structure.

The forward risk concentrates in one place. Roughly nineteen hours of unpriced information, an unresolved military exchange at a shipping chokepoint, an energy premium and untested hawkish rate pricing all meet a single opening auction rather than a continuous session. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday, so cash equities and the bond market are closed and the futures session that follows the reopen is shortened and thinner. That concentration is scored as a 20% Tail allowance in the 22:00 and 23:00 UTC slots, which maps to WATCH and yellow and forms the only published danger window, then steps down to 17%, 15% and 14%. It is a conditional gap-and-extension allowance, not an assertion that directional structure has been observed; if the reopening auction instead shows shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements, later assessments will revise those slots upward on observed evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 03:00 UTC on 5 September to 02:00 UTC on 6 September and lie entirely inside the CME weekend halt. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 4-5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from 03:00 UTC through 10:00 UTC, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and peaked at 57% at 20:00 UTC when the IRGC counter-claim and Iran's threat of more severe attacks were published. It then eased steadily to 53% by 02:00 UTC as the sequence went quiet, and the closing slot lowered Tail to 4% on that same decay. Confidence held in a narrow 85-86% band throughout: the assessment kept current verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and calendar coverage, but no live Nasdaq-100 price path existed in any of the 24 hours.
outlookSummary: Nineteen of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with Tail on the 5% closed-venue floor through the dormant hours, lifting from 13:00 UTC as a pre-auction gap allowance and reaching 14% in the last full hour of the halt. The final five slots are different: futures are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, so those hours are the first in which structure can exist. The reopening hour and the first full hour after it each carry a 20% Tail allowance, map to WATCH and yellow, and together form the only published danger window; the last three slots step back to 17%, 15% and 14% and to green on the assumption of an orderly auction into the shortened US Labor Day futures session. Stress opens at 56%, reaches a 54% low in the quiet Sunday hours, then rebuilds through the afternoon to a 72% peak at the reopen before easing to 65%. Confidence declines from 85% to 72% because every later slot rests on Friday-dated market evidence and on a geopolitical sequence whose latest step is still an unconfirmed IRGC claim.
